text: There is a slight improvement in the floods situation in Bagdad to-day, but 5,000 men are still working all night protecting the embankment.

label: text
text: Ladies of the Royal Family departed for the King's cotton estate, 100 miles north of Bagdad, but King Faisal himself found temporary accommodation in the house of a wealthy Jewish merchant of Bagdad.

label: text
text: Great alarm was caused this morning by a strong northerly breeze which raised a choppy sea in the huge flooded area outside Bagdad. Waves breaking against the embankment threatened to destroy it within a few hours with the dire results for Bagdad, but luckily the wind fell before the damage became irretrievable. During the crisis, however, £2,000 were expended in sandbags, the prices of which soared up, in an endeavour to keep the waves at bay.

text: He was a burglar.

label: text
text: After effecting an entrance into the bank he found his way easily enough to the strong room. When the light of the lantern fell on the door he saw this sign written in red letters:—

label: text
text: “Save your dynamite: This safe is not locked. Turn the knob and it will open.”

label: text
text:
For a moment he ruminated.
"Anyhow," he reflected, "there's no harm in trying it if it really is unlocked."

label: text
text: He grasped the knob and turned it.

label: text
text: Instantly the office was flooded with light, an alarm bell rang loudly, an electric shock rendered him helpless, while a panel in the wall opened and out rushed a bulldog which seized him firmly.

label: text
text: An hour later, when the cell door closed on him, he sighed:---

label: text
text: “I know what's wrong with me. I'm too trusting. I have too much faith in human nature.”

text: writing in the British Australian and New Zealand describes a new industry for Western Australia which may in future affect for good the British and other settlers in that region. It appears that sharks, those dreaded denizens of the ocean, infest those coasts in great numbers, and according to Dr Alfred Ehrenraith this fact may have great commercial importance. This research worker has found that the hides of sharks can be successfully tanned, an average of ten square feet being generally obtainable from this part of a shark. The leather is durable and suitable for soles of boots; a material from which soft leather for boot uppers is obtainable can also be produced from the shark's stomach. Besides this, from the shark's liver and intestines medical and other oils can be expressed glue can be made from its head; its teeth can be utilised by jewellers from its secretion of pancreatic acid, insulin a cure for diabetes can be manufactured, and its flesh and fine are edible. The shark is, in fact, now declared to be more valuable to man than a pig. The new venture in catching these monsters of the deep is to be launched states this writer, at Shark's Bay, about 800 miles from Fremantle.

text: LABOUR LEADERS LEAVE

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON SHORT OF CASH.

label: text
text: In order to attend the Second Chinese National Labour Mass Meeting to be held in Canton for ten days, starting from May 1, 1926, representatives (including ten employees of the Japanese owned mills) from the local labour organisations "have left secretly during the past few days. When the first mass meeting was convened last year, each representative from various cities was paid his travelling expenses to and from Canton by the Communist Headquarters in that city. But this year, in view of the shortage of funds by Canton Communists, representatives from local labour organisations were given $30 each as travelling expenses by their respective Workers' Union. It is feared that after the representatives return here from Canton, they will cause agitation among local labourers. Apart from anything of a political nature, a new movement aiming at improving living conditions of workers in general is expected to be promoted by them, thus appealing to public sympathy, according to the "Shanghai Mainichi."

Chicago, March 18.
A bit of the sen—1,000,000 gallons of genuine ocean water—is to be transported to Chicago.
Mr. George F. Morse, director of the $2,000,000 Shedd Aquarium, to be erected in Grant Park, is making a preliminary survey of the Atlantic, Pacific and Gulf coasts in search of a favourable spot, from which to obtain the sea water for the salt-water fish of the aquarium.
Synthetic salt-water lacks the organic content and chemical constituents of real ocean water without which salt-water fish cannot live, Mr. Morse said.
The entire shipment will require 125 railroad tank cura having a capacity of $8,000 gallons each. The $1,000,000 gallons will be stored in a huge reservoir.

label: text
text: "Once we have our full supply of salt-water," Mr. Morse stated, "we will be equipped for an indefinite period since the water can be used over and over again by virtue of a process of filtration and aeration. Evaporation will take place but this affects only the water and not the salts. We will simply add filtered water."

label: text
text: Some difficulty surrounds the search for an ideal spot from which to take the supply from the ocean, said the aquarium director. Water from an unpolluted place along the shore line is wanted, and the ideal location calls for a pier with railroad trackage so that the water may be pumped direct into the tank cars. Otherwise an additional handling by boats would be necessary. "We will select the shortest and easiest route available, all other things being equal, and ship the water about 10 cars at a time," Mr. Morse said.
